claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets are governed by interactions among lattice distortion, dislocation density, and stacking-fault energy.
Constituent identity and interactions influence lattice distortion.
Constituent identity and interactions influence dislocation density.
Constituent identity and interactions influence stacking-fault energy.
The investigated quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Systematically changing constituent identity while retaining equiatomic compositions and single-phase FCC structures provides the proposed intervention.
The intervention also varies constituent proportions while maintaining equiatomic composition.
Interactions among lattice distortion, dislocation density, and stacking-fault energy affect deformation behavior.
Interactions among lattice distortion, dislocation density, and stacking-fault energy affect failure behavior.
The investigated subsets will exhibit a 10–20% increase in yield strength relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline.
The investigated subsets will exhibit a 5–10% increase in ductility relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline.
The predicted strength and ductility increases will be accompanied by increased stacking-fault energy.
The predicted strength and ductility increases will be accompanied by increased dislocation density.
The hypothesis is limited to constituent variations and thermomechanical-processing conditions that preserve equiatomic composition and a single-phase FCC structure.
The quantitative relationship and individual contributions of lattice distortion, dislocation density, and stacking-fault energy remain uncertain.
Failure to obtain at least a 5% yield-strength increase and a 2% ductility increase relative to the quinary baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes varying constituent proportions while simultaneously requiring equiatomic composition. Within a fixed constituent set, proportions cannot be systematically varied while every constituent remains equiatomic; only constituent identity or constituent count can vary under that constraint.
